newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt operating surplus NZ$1.8 bn, 5 mths to Nov.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt operating surplus NZ$1.8 bn, 5 mths to Nov.

text.p: The New Zealand government said on Friday it posted an operating budget surplus of NZ$1.78 billion for the five months to November 30, 1996, against a forecast surplus of $1.51 billion.
Tax revenue was $114 million (0.8 percent) higher than forecast, largely due to higher than forecast non residents' withholding tax and source deductions revenue.
Expenses, excluding net foreign exchange gains, were $28 million (0.2 percent) lower than forecast, while non-tax revenue was $53 million (4.2 percent) greater than forecast.

The net surplus, less distributions, attributable to State- owned enterprises and Crown entities was $74 million (53.6 percent) above forecast, mainly due to higher than expected Crown entity net surpluses.
The Crown balance (net worth) at November 30 was NZ$5.3 billion, $263 million higher than forecast and $1.98 billion higher than at June 30.
Treasury said this was due to the $1.78 billion operating balance, combined with net asset revaluations of $196 million.
Net cash flows from operating and investing activities were $1.14 billion, compared with a forecast inflow of $971 million.
This was due largely to higher than forecast taxation receipts of $108 million, and lower than forecast cash disbursed to operations ($59 million).
The financial statements for the six months ended December 31, 1996, are required to be tabled in the House of Representatives before they are published.
